newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Autoliv acquisitions help profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Autoliv acquisitions help profits.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment maker Autoliv AB reported on Thursday a 13 percent rise in 1996 profits, saying the negative effects of a weaker crown were overcome by the positive effects of a handful of acquisitions.
Autoliv posted a profit after financial items of 1.15 billion crowns ($159 million) as sales in the year to December 31 rose 14 percent to 11.6 billion crowns.
Analysts said the result was much in line with market expectations and all eyes were on the soon-to-be-finalised merger with the automotive component unit of U.S. group Morton International Inc.
"The improvement was due largely to a higher degree of integration in operations and continued cost cutting," Autoliv said in a statement.
"A negative effect of a stronger Swedish crown was outweighed by the positive effect from a company acquisition," Autoliv said in a statement. Prices have continued to fall."
A Reuter poll of analysts found expectations of a profit after financial items of 1.16 billion crowns.
"If you take into account a non-recurring cost in the fourth quarter (of 10 million crowns) then the result was exactly in line with market expectations," analyst Jan Dworsky of Fiba told Reuters.
Autoliv's share price rose 2.5 crowns to 322.5 crowns after the earnings report was released but in later trade slipped back three crowns below Wednesday's closing price.

A company spokesman told Reuters the acquisition of two Swedish seat component companies -- now called Autoliv Hammarverken and Autoliv Mekan -- and French steering wheel company, Isodelta, helped the 1996 result.
An improved performance was noted in both of Autoliv's key areas during the year and particularly in the final months.
Sales of airbags rose by 13 percent to 5.5 billion crowns while the sale of seat belts rose by 15 percent to 6.1 billion crowns. Fourth quarter sales rose 26 percent from a year ago.
Autoliv said the increase in sales outperformed growth in the most important market -- the manufacture of light vehicles in Europe -- which rose an estimated three percent in 1996.
But analysts said the market had limited interest in Autoliv's 1996 earnings and the focus was now on the merger with Morton for which a prospectus will be released in March.

The merger, first mooted in September, will create one of the world's largest airbag operations, called Autoliv Inc. Sales will total $3 billion and the company will have a staff of 15,000 in Europe, Japan and the U.S..

"There have been few details presented from the company so far as regards the merger and the market is eagerly awaiting the prospectus to get some more details on how large the goodwill will be and to quantify the synergies," Dworsky said.
Analyst Gustav von Essen from brokerage Carnegie was very positive about the merger.
"I think the merger with Morton is a perfect match. It will create a very strong group with global coverage which is very important," von Essen told Reuters.
Autoliv proposed a dividend of 2.75 crowns a share which is a 22 percent rise from last year's dividend of 2.25 crowns.
